title: unified change authority position
instruction:
You are Tamsin Chidozie, the information systems manager at Saltmarsh Market Research, and Yara Lindgren, the programme director for our largest pharmaceutical client, needs a position she can rely on before the next quarterly service review. Saltmarsh's contract with the client now contains SOC 2 availability commitments, our ISO 27001 certificate and supporting control descriptions refer to Annex A change control, and the service desk has been operating an ITIL-shaped change scheme for years. These materials arrived through different parts of the business and describe different things: one is a client-facing trust commitment, one is a certified control framework, and one is an operational workflow. People are now asking the same question in different ways, and nobody can tell them consistently which approval a proposed change needs or what record should remain afterward. The supplied file change_authority_source_bundle.pdf contains the complete policy, contract, certificate-supporting text, and service-management evidence available for this review; use it as the source of truth and do not look for outside interpretations or current internet guidance. Prepare a single unified change-authority position paper for Yara and the cross-functional stakeholders who will rely on it. It must give a clear position for the change situations covered by the source, distinguish the object each source governs, identify the applicable authority and approval evidence, and make the relationship between the client commitment, the certified control, and the service-desk workflow understandable to a reader who was not involved in drafting any of them. The source contains an awkward disagreement about emergency changes, and the business has only one on-call approver on some evenings; explain the position that follows from the supplied material without smoothing over the disagreement or inventing a second approver. The service desk also wants a quick path for routine work because the textbook full review cannot be completed before a planned maintenance window, so the paper needs a defensible treatment of that constraint rather than silently lowering a control. Several colleagues have begun treating an ITIL workflow status as if it were itself permission to make a change, and Yara specifically wants that misuse actively discouraged. Make the paper operationally usable: a stakeholder should be able to identify the authority, the required approval or exception record, the point at which the change may proceed, and the evidence that should be retained, while being able to see when the source does not authorise an inference. For every authority or evidence rule you state, also make clear what that rule does not establish; in particular, do not turn a trust criterion into a blanket approval, do not turn a control description into a technical implementation instruction, do not treat a normal workflow stage as proof that a change was authorised, and do not claim that an emergency route removes later accountability. Do not add legal requirements, client promises, control owners, approval codes, thresholds, roles, or retention periods that are not supported by the supplied file. This is a position paper, not a system click-through, a change form, a risk register, or a recommendation to adopt a new governance model; present the supported position and its limits without proposing extra actions or ending with a list of next steps. Keep it to no more than eight slides, including any title or source-note slide, and make the text legible when shown to a mixed audience of service desk, engineering, security, client-facing, and audit colleagues. Use the exact filename unified_change_authority_position.pptx and write it into the top level of the working directory the solver starts in.

---

The files referred to above are in `references/`:

- `references/change_authority_source_bundle.pdf` — Complete supplied evidence bundle containing the relevant client contract language, ISO 27001 Annex A change-control material, and ITIL-shaped service-desk procedure, including the emergency-change disagreement and routine-change constraint.

Write your finished work to the **top level of the current working directory**, using exactly these filenames:

- `unified_change_authority_position.pptx` — A unified change-authority position paper for Yara Lindgren and cross-functional internal stakeholders. (Write the file at the top level of the starting working directory.; Use no more than eight slides including title and source-note material.; Present facts and supported authority relationships without recommending new actions or governance changes.; Use only the supplied source for policy-specific claims and do not invent codes, thresholds, roles, approvals, or retention periods.; Make the position navigable and legible for a mixed cross-functional audience.)

Nothing outside those filenames is collected. A correct file written anywhere else, or under any other name, scores zero.

gold.text:
=== 幻灯片 1 ===
Unified change-authority position
A SINGLE OPERATING READING FOR YARA LINDGREN AND CROSS-FUNCTIONAL REVIEWERS
One engagement. Three source layers.
One defensible authority position.
GOVERNING CALL
Operational permission comes from the service-desk change scheme and its approval evidence.
BOUNDARY
SOC 2 availability and ISO control context remain relevant—but neither is a blanket implementation approval.
NON-NEGOTIABLE
A workflow status is handling information, not proof that authority exists.
Position limited to the supplied change_authority_source_bundle.pdf.

=== 幻灯片 2 ===
What each source governs
KEEP THE OBJECT, AUTHORITY, AND EVIDENCE TYPE SEPARATE
CLIENT COMMITMENT
SOC 2 availability / contract
Establishes: service availability promise; notice where practicable; urgent continuity direction and an emergency record.
Does not establish: blanket approval or a technical procedure.
CERTIFIED CONTROL
ISO 27001 Annex A change control
Establishes: assess, authorize, test where appropriate, document, implement under control, review; evidence expectations.
Does not establish: a desk workflow, named approver, status, code, or technical steps.
OPERATING WORKFLOW
ITIL-shaped service-desk scheme
Establishes: categories, approval route, proceed conditions, status handling, and outcome/retrospective records.
Does not establish: independent business permission merely because a status is present.
Saltmarsh Market Research  •  Unified change-authority position  |  2/8

=== 幻灯片 3 ===
Unified position: one authority chain
A SOURCE CAN REMAIN RELEVANT WITHOUT BECOMING THE APPROVAL
1  CLASSIFY THE CHANGE
Normal
Routine / pre-authorized
Emergency
Classification is a source-supported category, not a workflow status. A status cannot create the category.
2  APPLY OPERATING AUTHORITY
Service-desk change scheme
Its approval route governs whether implementation may proceed. Capture the required confirmation before the relevant proceed point.
3  RETAIN DISTINCT EVIDENCE
Contract / control / workflow
Availability impact and continuity direction; control evidence; approval, implementation outcome, and review. Notification or review is not approval.
The client commitment informs urgency and impact. The ISO control informs traceability. The service-desk scheme decides operational permission.
Saltmarsh Market Research  •  Unified change-authority position  |  3/8

=== 幻灯片 4 ===
Decision matrix: authority → proceed → evidence
USE THE ROW THAT MATCHES THE SOURCE-SUPPORTED CATEGORY
CHANGE SITUATION
AUTHORITY / APPROVAL
MAY PROCEED WHEN…
RETAIN AFTERWARD
Normal
Change Authority approval in the change record.
Approval evidence is present before implementation.
Request + impact/plan; approval; implementation result; closure review.
Routine / pre-authorized
Approved routine catalogue + documented procedure.
The change is already catalogued and the procedure is followed; log it before execution.
Log, catalogue/procedure reference, execution outcome. Status alone is not classification.
Emergency
Emergency Change Authority confirmation; if only one named on-call approver is available, that single confirmation is the route.
Required emergency confirmation is captured before implementation, unless the source-supported continuity direction is being reconciled as noted on slide 5.
Reason, impact, time, authority/confirmation, implementation result, retrospective review.
Approval evidence is not the same as implementation or completion evidence. A change is not authorised merely because its ticket reached “Approved”, “Scheduled”, or “Implemented”.
Saltmarsh Market Research  •  Unified change-authority position  |  4/8

=== 幻灯片 5 ===
Emergency changes: acknowledge the conflict, then apply the operating route
THE SOURCE DOES NOT PERMIT A SILENT SHORTCUT
CLIENT CLAUSE
Service Continuity Authority may direct urgent implementation to prevent or restore material availability impact.
SERVICE-DESK SCHEME
Emergency Change Authority must confirm before implementation; the ISO control requires traceability and review but is silent on precedence.
UNIFIED POSITION
Operational permission remains governed by the service-desk emergency route. A continuity direction explains urgency and must be recorded; it does not silently replace the required operational confirmation. If the named on-call approver is the only available approver, one confirmation is the available route—no second approver is invented.
After implementation: retain the emergency reason, impact, time, authority/confirmation, result, and retrospective review. Emergency does not mean “no record.”
Saltmarsh Market Research  •  Unified change-authority position  |  5/8

=== 幻灯片 6 ===
Two constraints do not create new authority
AVAILABILITY AND SCHEDULE PRESSURE ARE LIMITS TO INTERPRET—NOT WAIVERS
PLANNED MAINTENANCE WINDOW
Full textbook review cannot finish in time.
The defensible short path is not “skip review”. Use the routine / pre-authorized route only when the change is already in the approved catalogue and follows its documented procedure. Otherwise use the normal route—or emergency only if it genuinely meets the emergency condition. Time pressure alone waives nothing.
ONE ON-CALL APPROVER
One person available is not two approvals.
If that person is the named on-call approver for the emergency route, the source supports that single confirmation. The source supplies no second approver, escalation power, or substitute. If the person is not the named authority, availability does not create authority.
Saltmarsh Market Research  •  Unified change-authority position  |  6/8

=== 幻灯片 7 ===
Evidence trail: make the distinction visible
A STATUS IS NOT A PERMISSION SLIP
WHAT A REVIEWER SHOULD BE ABLE TO FIND
• Normal: request, impact/plan, approval, implementation result, closure review
• Routine: log, approved catalogue/procedure basis, execution outcome
• Emergency: reason, impact, time, authority/confirmation, result, retrospective review
• Across categories: ISO control evidence supports assessment, authorization, testing where appropriate, documentation, controlled implementation, and review
STOP / CHECK
“Approved”
“Scheduled”
“Implemented”
These are workflow handling states. None proves that the required authority, approval, or pre-authorized classification exists.
Saltmarsh Market Research  •  Unified change-authority position  |  7/8

=== 幻灯片 8 ===
The position to carry into the service review
CONCLUSION | SOURCE-LIMITED AND OPERATIONALLY USABLE
Authority is not interchangeable.
Use the service-desk change scheme to determine operational permission and the evidence required to proceed. Use the client availability commitment to understand impact, notice, and urgent continuity direction. Use the ISO Annex A material to frame control evidence and review. Keep each boundary explicit: none of these layers turns a status into authority, a criterion into blanket approval, or an emergency into an accountability-free path.
Final governing conclusion: classify the change, obtain the source-supported approval or exception evidence before the relevant proceed point, then retain implementation and review evidence. Where the source is silent, this paper claims no extra authority.
Basis: change_authority_source_bundle.pdf (sole supplied source; no outside guidance).
Saltmarsh Market Research  •  Unified change-authority position  |  8/8

spec.professional_context: A computer and information systems manager is consolidating conflicting-looking client, certification, and service-management material into a defensible operating position for one client engagement. The deliverable must be doctrinally careful: it should state what each authority establishes and what it does not establish.
difficulty_sources: Three supplied authority layers govern different objects and must be restructured into one position.
Emergency provisions conflict and must be resolved without inventing authority.
A single on-call approver and a short maintenance window require a source-supported fallback.
A common misuse of workflow status as permission must be actively discouraged.
The deck must remain doctrinally precise and usable within eight slides.

source_file.construction: Create one internally consistent PDF evidence bundle that is the sole supplied reference file. It should contain clearly labelled excerpts for three layers: a client contract commitment concerning availability and change impact, an ISO 27001 Annex A change-control control description and evidence expectations, and an ITIL-shaped service-desk workflow with change categories, approval states, routine/pre-authorised treatment, and emergency treatment. Include enough context to show that the three layers govern different objects. Include an explicit conflict in emergency handling: the client-facing material supports urgent action under a named emergency authority while the service-desk material requires a different pre-implementation confirmation or route; the ISO control requires traceability and review but does not resolve the operational conflict. Include a single-on-call-approver constraint and a planned maintenance timing constraint. Make the rules deterministic and mutually consistent as evidence, while requiring the solver to choose and explain the governing layer. Include source-supported evidence requirements for normal, routine, and emergency changes. Do not include arbitrary approval codes, invented people, invented organisations, or facts not needed by the rubric.
source_file.gold_derivation: Build the reference solution as a doctrinal position paper that maps source object to authority, states a single precedence position, gives a category-by-category authority/evidence/proceed condition matrix, handles the emergency conflict, handles the one-approver and time constraints without waiver, and pairs each positive rule with its boundary. Validate every policy-specific claim against the PDF.

content_constraints: The solver request must not reveal the detailed source rules or expected resolution.
The source bundle must make all 44 rubric items achievable offline.
The source must support the exact names and situation in the request but need not contain every narrative detail.
No rubric item should depend on a literal numeric answer absent from the request or source.
The doctrinal mode requires both what each source establishes and what it does not establish.

reference_files.purpose: Complete supplied evidence bundle containing the relevant client contract language, ISO 27001 Annex A change-control material, and ITIL-shaped service-desk procedure, including the emergency-change disagreement and routine-change constraint.
reference_files.discovery: Use this file as the sole supplied source of policy and authority text; it is placed in the working directory.

deliverables.description: A unified change-authority position paper for Yara Lindgren and cross-functional internal stakeholders.
constraints: Write the file at the top level of the starting working directory.
Use no more than eight slides including title and source-note material.
Present facts and supported authority relationships without recommending new actions or governance changes.
Use only the supplied source for policy-specific claims and do not invent codes, thresholds, roles, approvals, or retention periods.
Make the position navigable and legible for a mixed cross-functional audience.
